rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday rendering when you mean telephone someone.

example.english: I’ll ring you in a bit.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zan6 gaan1 daa2 din6 waa2 bei2 nei5

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose noun for a telephone call.

example.english: I got a ring from you just now.
example.jyutping: ngo5 tau4 sin1 sau1 dou2 nei5 go3 din6 waa2

rows.note: Use this everyday word for jewelry worn on a finger.

example.english: This ring was a gift from my boyfriend.
example.traditional: 呢隻戒指係我男朋友送畀我㗎。
example.jyutping: ni1 zek3 gaai3 zi2 hai6 ngo5 naam4 pang4 jau5 sung3 bei2 ngo5 gaa3

rows.note: Use this when a bell, phone, or similar object itself is producing the ringing sound, rather than when someone makes it ring.

example.english: Listen, the phone’s about to ring.
example.traditional: 你聽吓，部電話就嚟響喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 teng1 haa5 bou6 din6 waa2 zau6 lai4 hoeng2 laa3

rows.note: Use this for the sound made by a bell or church bell.

example.english: The church bell's ring has sounded.
example.jyutping: gaau3 tong4 ge3 zung1 seng1 hoeng2 hei2 laa3

rows.note: Use this for a circular group or a band of material encircling something.

example.english: There is a black ring of trim around the waist of this skirt.
example.traditional: 呢條裙腰有一圈黑色花邊。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 kwan4 jiu1 jau5 jat1 hyun1 hak1 sik1 faa1 bin1

rows.note: Use this for the common doorbell situation, when someone presses the bell to make it ring.

example.english: Ring the doorbell and I’ll open the door.
example.jyutping: nei5 gam6 mun4 zung1 ngo5 heoi3 hoi1 mun4

rows.note: Use this when judging how something sounds, especially whether it sounds true or plausible.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gong2 faat3 teng1 lok6 gei2 ci5 zan1
